subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs use `deleteAfterRun` as a per-run session cleanup default, or should recurring `deleteAfterRun: true` be rejected as a one-shot-only lifecycle flag?
rationale: Both open PRs are internally plausible but encode opposite public cron semantics, and automation should not choose a persisted lifecycle contract for existing users.

options.title: Support recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require a persisted-row, load, or doctor path for existing omitted jobs before merge.

options.title: Reject recurring delete-after-run
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation path after its Gateway/UI compatibility blockers are fixed.

options.title: Fresh creates only
options.body: Accept this PR as a new-job default only and explicitly document that existing omitted jobs need operator migration or a separate repair.

recommendation.title: Support recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require a persisted-row, load, or doctor path for existing omitted jobs before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans cron normalization and persisted store behavior, where the strongest recent source-history signal points to steipete.
